notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/threadhero.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/threadhero.md at e7ed622 (“docs: publish 19 Component Fix fixes on jfs-components dbe0e02”). The guide's Sources note was checked on 28 October 2026 on the installed build itself (jfs-components 0.1.78, the 27 October build: mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02, Biscuit's main at dbe0e02), so items citing it carry 2026-10-28 and 0.1.78-dbe0e02. The evidence's dbe0e02 section (#397 verified 27 October on dbe0e02, closed by Marcin, published 28 October) replaces its 25 October sections (0.1.78-c8526ae) where they differ; items from that section carry 2026-10-27 and 0.1.78-dbe0e02, and lines from the 25 October sections carry 2026-10-25 and 0.1.78-c8526ae and are used only where the installed source still agrees. Installed ThreadHero.tsx (137 lines), react-utils' cloneChildrenWithModes and resolveTruncation, typography's safeTextLineHeight and the threadHero/* and avatar size tokens (through the package's own resolver) match every guide sentence used here, read from source, not run: the props are title (default “Subhash Rajan”), subtitle (default “Banking name: SHIVASHANKAR RAJAN”), caption (no default), renderAvatar (no default; undefined, null, false and '' show nothing), modes, style (spread last on the root) and disableTruncation, with no onPress, testID, accessibility props or children; the root is a View, a centred column with an 8 px gap (threadHero/gap) and no width, holding a centred, full-width column with a 2 px gap (threadHero/details/gap) for the avatar, name and banking name, then the caption; the name is 16 px weight 600 on a 20 px line (#191b1e), centred, with no line limit, so it wraps; the banking name and caption are 12 px weight 500 on an 18 px line (#5d5d61), one line with a tail ellipsis unless disableTruncation; title, subtitle and caption render only when non-empty (ThreadHero.tsx:123-134); every threadHero/* token is a one-mode literal (Thread Hero / Output), so no mode changes the hero's text; renderAvatar is cloned with { ...heroModes, ...avatarModes } (react-utils.ts:59-66), so the avatar's own modes win and fragments are unwrapped; Avatar Size defaults to L, 42 px (M 36, S 29) through context/avatar/size; an Avatar with no props is style Image with the bundled photo, and it is pressable only with onPress. Heights add up as 42 + 2 + 20 + 2 + 18 + 8 + 18 = 110, 84 without a caption and 40 without avatar and caption. No guide sentence is contradicted by the installed source; the Sizing sentence names the 2 px once, though the same 2 px also separates the name from the banking name, which is how its parts make 110 (the entry keeps the guide's wording). Not used, because the dbe0e02 section replaces them: the 25 October Contract lines that renderAvatar's own modes are replaced (“on the Avatar itself it's overwritten”), the published stories' nonexistent Avatar props, the MDX's “all three lines ellipsize”, and the MDX Anatomy specimen and Code Connect points (#397, closed). Not recorded: style (the building rules keep style off Coin components); the evidence's colours; Biscuit's handwritten MDX lines the evidence quotes (not the signed-in user, ProfileCard; not a payment result, StatusHero; its content lines), since the guide does not say them; the Storybook story list, Hosting and Limits. Accessibility stays empty: the guide gives none, and the evidence only says the hero has no accessibility props and its avatar is an image on the web; screen-reader names are not gaps in this pack. Avatar Size is created as an evidence mode fact (create: true): ThreadHero's own mode metadata lists no collections, but the hero passes its modes to the avatar (the dbe0e02 section), and its values are the package's Avatar Size collection. The two required content rules rest on the title and subtitle defaults (props facts), as in the MerchantProfile entry. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every hero and column) and no Avatar Size (L, 42 px, is the default and Figma's; no guide sentence says some content needs another), and the slotted Avatar carries no modes. Avatar has no entry in this pack; the examples use it because renderAvatar is the hero's only way to show an avatar and the guide fills it with a Monogram Avatar and asks for initials without a photo (its Don't shows the default Avatar's stranger photo), as the BrandChip entry does. The In context example drops the guide's two Transaction Bubbles (no entry in this pack), their widths and the VStack with Slot gap XL around them, so it shows the hero alone; the Wrapped example drops the 240 px column (a style width). Copy is the guide's own (RV, Rahul Verma, Banking name: RAHUL KUMAR VERMA, +91 98765 43210; VR, Venkatasubramanian Ramakrishnan, Banking name: VENKATASUBRAMANIAN RAMAKRISHNAN, venkatasubramanian.r@okjio). Left out of examples (the pack allows three): Without a caption, Without an avatar, Cut, Phone number and UPI ID (their copy is in content good), the playground and the Don'ts. Gaps are the two Figma differences still open: Figma's nested Avatar against renderAvatar with no default (the Sources note), and Figma's caption on by default and 360 px width against a caption only when passed and no width of its own (the 25 October Discrepancies line, no ticket; still true in the installed source). Sorting (batch 8): the cross-check found that the default-avatar Don't also read as ruling out the Monogram avatar the Do recommends; it now says an Avatar left with no photo and not set to Monogram. It also found the Avatar Size fact calling L the default and Figma's size, which the evidence does not say; the description now gives only the evidence's S 29 and M 36 and Figma's 42 px (the default L is the package collection's own default mode). A second cross-check found that the phone-number format, the caption under the guide's Phone number example, was stated as a rule for every number; it now keeps the example's context.

evidenceFacts.name: title
evidenceFacts.description: The name: 16 px Semibold (600) on a 20 px line, centred; it wraps, with no line limit.

evidenceFacts.name: subtitle
evidenceFacts.description: The banking name: 12 px Medium on an 18 px line, grey, centred, one line with an ellipsis. An empty string hides it; left out, it shows the default.

evidenceFacts.name: caption
evidenceFacts.description: No default: 12 px Medium on an 18 px line, grey, one line with an ellipsis, 8 px below the banking name; hidden when not passed.
evidenceFacts.quote: `caption` (no default): 12/18 Medium `#5d5d61`, one line with ellipsis, 8 px below; hidden when not passed.

evidenceFacts.name: renderAvatar
evidenceFacts.description: No default avatar. The avatar gets the hero's modes and its own modes win; fragments and arrays get the hero's modes too; false shows no avatar.
evidenceFacts.quote: Fragments and arrays get the hero's modes; `renderAvatar={false}` shows no avatar.

evidenceFacts.name: modes
evidenceFacts.description: No mode changes the hero's own text: its tokens have one mode. The hero passes its modes to the avatar.
evidenceFacts.quote: no mode changes the hero's own text (one-mode literals)

evidenceFacts.name: disableTruncation
evidenceFacts.description: The banking name and the caption wrap instead of ending in an ellipsis; the name wraps either way.

evidenceFacts.name: Avatar Size
evidenceFacts.description: Not read by the hero's own text: the hero passes its modes to the avatar, so Avatar Size on the hero sizes it (a hero at S gives a 29 px avatar), and an Avatar Size set on the avatar itself wins (an avatar at M gives 36 px whatever the hero's size). Figma's nested Avatar is 42 px.
evidenceFacts.quote: an avatar set to Size S stays 29 px, and a hero at S with an avatar at M gives 36.

gaps.text: Figma's Thread Hero has Title, Subtitle and Caption text properties, a caption switch and a nested Avatar; the package has no avatar unless you pass one in renderAvatar.

gaps.text: Figma's caption shows by default and its Thread Hero is 360 px wide; the package hides the caption until you pass one and has no width of its own (it hugs its text).
